newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine industrial output rises 6.9 pct in Feb.
newsitem.headline: Argentine industrial output rises 6.9 pct in Feb.

text.p: Argentine industrial production in February rose 6.9 percent on the same month last year, the Economy Ministry announced Monday.
For the first two months of the year the output increase on Jan-Feb 1996 was 7.0 percent.

The February advance, which is the eleventh straight month of positive industrial output performances, compares to a 7.2 percent rise in industrial output in January and a 3.5 percent year-on-year drop in February last year.
Month-on-month, the non-seasonally-adjusted February rise was 3.2 percent and seasonally-adjusted it was 3.7 percent.

The Economy Ministry emphasized auto-related output in the first two months of 1997, especially tires and synthetic rubber. There was also growth in building materials and in wheat milling for exports to Brazil.
The biggest falls for January-February were for oil crushers but they were also recovering by late February, the ministry said.

The ministry also released data of its monthly survey of 83 leading companies showing 40.9 percent believed March would see a rise in domestic demand for their products, against just 9.1 percent who are pessimistic for the month.
At the same time 35.8 percent foresee increased export demand versus just 4.5 percent expecting lower exports.
"There is another interesting fact about companies' credit needs -- 61.5 percent satisfy their financial needs locally, while 28.9 percent resort to international credit," it said.
